subject.title: fix(doctor): preserve allowlist entries for version-bound runtime plugins during stale config scan

question: Should doctor permanently exempt every version-bound runtime plugin ID from stale allowlist cleanup, or should preservation be limited to a pending or failed install/backfill lifecycle?
rationale: Both behaviors are plausible compatibility policies, but they differ in whether obsolete IDs can remain forever; repository policy requires an explicit owner decision for compatibility fallbacks and migration lifetimes.

options.title: Bound preservation to installation
options.body: Route allow-only version-bound IDs through the missing-plugin install/backfill flow and preserve them only while installation is pending or failed.

options.title: Declare a permanent exemption
options.body: Keep the caller-level exemption, document that version-bound runtime IDs are never stale, and add focused upgrade and cleanup-contract tests.

options.title: Pause for packaging resolution
options.body: Hold this PR if the actual defect is release packaging or backfill metadata rather than stale-config sequencing.

recommendation.title: Bound preservation to installation
recommendation.body: Route allow-only version-bound IDs through the missing-plugin install/backfill flow and preserve them only while installation is pending or failed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent CLI/runtime work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for deciding the doctor and runtime-plugin upgrade contract.
